doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: The bootleg Milan album with Louis and Tyree Glenn
summary: A black-market double album of Marty and Tyree Glenn with Louis Armstrong, perhaps because both took encores.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well I have to get to Louis Armstrong.
And I see he was lucky enough to get his name on an album with you.

That’s a black market album you know, from Milano. And I had a friend of mine, I was working at Eddie Condon’s on 54th Street one night, and I saw a friend of mine who was a distributor. Joe Muranyi sent me this, the clarinet player, he sent me this. He said, “I’ve got an album of you and Louis and Tyree.” I said, “what do you mean? Send me the album.” I said I can’t believe this, it’s double album, see? It’s got our pictures inside and everything. But the reason I think they picked Tyree and me was because he and I were the only guys in the band who did an encore. See and when we did concerts with Louis, if you got an exceptionally big hand, they’d say do another chorus of that, Pops. Do an © Fillius Jazz Archive -24-

encore, do something else. You could either do the same thing over, or play another song. So Tyree and I both got big enough hands that he would say do another song. So they figured in Italy, in Milano, they said these guys must be the big stars in the band, because they’re the only ones that did an extra chorus. That’s the only way I can figure it out. Because why would they do that? And that’s a funny story. Was that after Charlie Barnet? No after Charlie Barnet I went with Gene Krupa’s band.
